UT-2026-SB151.policyArea: Appropriations, Department of Public Safety, Government Operations (State Issues)
UT-2026-SB151.aiSummary: Utah passed a bill that changes how some public safety and highway funds can be used. It adds state money to a motor vehicle safety account, which can help pay for Highway Patrol troopers, overtime, and equipment. It also lets money from the Transportation Investment Fund of 2005 be used to run a state highway, including traffic law enforcement, if that highway was built, rebuilt, or renovated with that fund. The bill was signed into law and includes $2,000,000 in operating and capital funds, plus $3,000,000 in restricted fund and account transfers for fiscal year 2027.

UT-2026-HB102.policyArea: Criminal Procedure, Government Records, Judicial Operations
UT-2026-HB102.aiSummary: The bill lets crime victims ask to use their initials instead of their name in certain public criminal justice records for offenses on or after July 1, 2026. Agencies, courts, and related offices would still have to keep the victim’s name and give it to a court if ordered. It also keeps victim address and contact details private in court unless the victim agrees or a judge orders release for a strong need. The law takes effect on May 6, 2026, and it was signed by the governor.

UT-2026-HB312.policyArea: Education, K-12 Education, Local Education Agencies (LEAs)
UT-2026-HB312.aiSummary: Signed into law, this measure changes Utah school curriculum rules. It requires more social studies teaching, including American self-government, government systems, founding documents, U.S. history, and constitutional government, and it sets new rules for literacy coaches and early reading support. It also lets local school agencies decide whether some applied crafts and technical arts classes count for fine arts credit, and it phases in some elementary social studies rules by July 1, 2031.

UT-2026-HB204.policyArea: Colleges and Universities, Education, Higher Education
UT-2026-HB204.aiSummary: The bill expands rules that let Utah college students ask for help with class work when it conflicts with their sincerely held religious or conscience beliefs. It also bars instructors from forcing students to take public positions on a matter of public concern and requires schools to set up notice, review, and reporting steps. It was signed into law and takes effect on May 6, 2026.
